about.title: Windsor Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Windsor's mix of shopping centers along Old Redwood Highway, residential complexes, and older sidewalks near the town green means falls happen for a range of reasons — wet flooring, uneven pavement, poor lighting, or neglected stairways. Under California law, proving a premises liability claim usually comes down to whether the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it in time. That's why documentation matters so much: photos of the hazard, witness names, and any store or building surveillance footage can make a real difference before it's deleted or overwritten. If you were injured on someone else's property in Windsor, our team can evaluate what happened and explain your options at no cost. There's no obligation, and we only get paid if you recover compensation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to Us About a Windsor Fall

items.title: Notice Has to Be Established
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We can help identify inspection records, prior complaints, or maintenance logs that speak to that.

items.title: Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Surveillance footage from a Windsor business or apartment complex is often overwritten within days or weeks, so an early request to preserve it can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Eliminate, Recovery
items.desc: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the fall, though your share of fault will factor into the final amount.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Windsor?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a claim under California law. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a town building or park, the deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim filing. Because of these differences, it helps to get an evaluation sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I fell at a business off Old Redwood Highway and no one else saw it happen?
items.answer: Witnesses help, but they aren't the only way to prove a claim. Store or building surveillance video, incident reports, and the physical condition of the area at the time can all support what happened. We can advise on how to request that evidence before it's lost.

items.question: Will it hurt my claim if I was partly at fault for the fall?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California follows a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility for the accident. Your total recovery would simply be adjusted to reflect your percentage of fault.
